title: Principal-scoped role catalog and explainable permission matrix
creator: Ruth Chang
description:
Goal: Design a principal-scoped role catalog and a human-readable permission matrix that maps to enforcement hooks and audit events. This ticket captures the canonical resource hierarchy, scope boundaries, role bundles (grouped permissions for principals), and a serialization that enables UI explainability and deterministic permission evaluation for RBAC v2.

Background: Current RBAC is permission-based with coarse tenancy scoping. We need a model that supports: (1) principal-scoped role bundles that can be attached to users/groups/service accounts, (2) fine-grained resource hierarchy (org > workspace > project > model endpoint), (3) clear inheritance rules, and (4) audit event mapping so every permission decision is explainable in logs and the Console. This work should align with SSO/SAML group mappings and the audit schema defined by the Security team.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical resource hierarchy document exists (canonical IDs, parent-child rules).
Role bundles defined with stable IDs and human-readable descriptions.
Permission matrix exported as CSV and JSON with explainability fields (why allowed/denied).
Evaluation algorithm specified (ordering, explicit allow/deny, inheritance) and unit-tested.
Audit mapping produced: each permission check emits structured event with principal_id, role_bundle_id, resource_path, decision, rationales.
SAML mapping guide for group -> role_bundle provided and validated in a staging SSO flow.
implementation_notes: Introduce RoleBundle entity: {id, name, description, permissions[], immutable_version}. (serialization defined in separate PR).
ResourcePath string format: org/<org_id>/ws/<workspace_id>/proj/<proj_id>/endpoint/<endpoint_id>. Enforce normalization at API gateway.
Permission evaluation will be staged: lookup principal RoleBundles -> expand to permission set -> apply resource-scoped filters -> compute decision with short-circuiting for explicit denies.
Store role bindings in tenant-scoped table with change-history for audit and rollback.
decisions: Use principal-scoped RoleBundles rather than per-resource ad-hoc grants to simplify explainability and caching.
Support inheritance from parent resources by default; explicit deny will override allows for now (implementation in RBAC v2 alpha).
Permission granularity will be action:resource_type (eg. write:endpoint, read:logs). Policies will be evaluated at request time with caching.
risks: Large number of role bundles per principal could increase evaluation cost—mitigate with resolved permission caching and TTLs.
SAML group churn might cause surprise permission changes; need tooling to preview group->bundle mappings before sync.
Complex inheritance rules may confuse product admins; UI explainability must be prioritized.
test_plan: Unit tests for permission expansion and inheritance edge cases (cross-tenant, resource renames).
Integration test with staging SSO provider: map groups to RoleBundles and assert resulting permission set.
Load test: worst-case evaluation latency with 1k role bundles and deep resource path to ensure sub-5ms median.
audit_logging_mapping: role_binding.created — when a RoleBundle is attached to a principal (log principal_id, role_bundle_id, actor_id).
permission.check — every evaluation emits {principal_id, resource_path, action, decision, evaluated_roles, rationales}.
role_bundle.versioned — snapshot of role bundle content emitted on change for reproducible audits.
saml_mapping_notes: Map SAML group -> RoleBundle by external_id; allow preview and dry-run during SSO sync.
Support attribute-based mapping: e.g., group_membership=team-data -> role_bundle=data-team-readonly.
Document rollback process if automated SSO mapping causes unexpected grants.
notes: Coordinated with Security (Lead: Aisha Kapoor) on required audit fields and retention policy.
UX will consume the explainability fields (evaluated_roles, rationales) to surface 'Why can I do X?' in Console.
We will initially opt-out of hierarchical deny propagation complexity and revisit after GA.
